public_messages: [Imani Okafor]: Based on the evidence, issuing a qualified opinion is the only acceptable course of action. The engagement team's assessment of material overstatement in receivables, supported by aging analysis and collectibility concerns, necessitates a qualified opinion per PCAOB standards.  Maintaining auditor independence requires us to prioritize the integrity of the audit opinion over preserving a client relationship. A clean opinion on financials with unresolved material misstatements creates unacceptable audit quality and litigation risks that the committee must seriously consider.

Issuing a qualified opinion is not only the correct course of action under PCAOB standards but also essential to maintaining auditor independence and upholding audit quality. A clean opinion in the face of such material misstatement would expose the firm to unacceptable litigation and reputational risks.  Preserving the client relationship cannot outweigh our ethical and professional obligations.
